threads.body: [Testing] Each worker reads the published reference rather than observing the helper bundle its transformation used. The test would still pass if a competing transformation incorrectly used its own unpublished bundle. Capture the bundle returned to or consumed by each transformation and assert that all transformations use the same instance during concurrent initialization.

replies.body: Fixed in a5ed1e9a666dacaa9935364889e685254bd6fffe. Each worker now captures the bundle passed to its ASM visitor factory during a real transformation, then compares that captured instance with the published bundle. The assertion no longer rereads the shared reference as the worker's result, so consuming an unpublished bundle fails it. The initialization algorithm is unchanged.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly to address the concurrency-test gap identified in review https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20964#discussion_r4373121251.

The original assignment requires concurrent first transformations to use the one published helper bundle and its shared injectors. In FieldBackedImplementationInstallerTest.concurrentTransformationsUseTheSameHelpers, each worker currently transforms and then returns installer.generatedClasses.get(). Those assertions only observe the published reference, not the bundle returned to or consumed by that transformation. They would still pass if a losing initializer incorrectly used its own unpublished bundle.

Strengthen this focused regression coverage so concurrent initialization observes the actual bundle returned to or consumed by each caller, checks that every caller uses the published instance, and can detect an incorrect losing-CAS return. Keep the existing real-transformation laziness/reuse coverage. Use the smallest repository-appropriate test seam if needed, without introducing public API, production initialization locks, or a separate implementation of the algorithm under test. Preserve the measured lazy-generation algorithm and all existing field injection, shared fallback storage, bootstrap injection ordering, and supported-Java behavior. Do not broaden the change into benchmark tooling or unrelated cleanup.

Run the narrow javaagent-tooling Spotless application before the focused unit tests. Run supported-Java coverage appropriate to the result, including -PtestJavaVersion=8 where feasible. Report actual outcomes and any blockers. Do not modify PR title or description, create another PR, or post replies to human reviewers.

@copilot Simplify the focused virtual-field initialization tests in this existing PR directly. The user asked, "Any simplification or reduction that's worth doing?" about javaagent-tooling/src/unitTests/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/tooling/field/FieldBackedImplementationInstallerTest.java and authorized the following agreed reduction through /cloud.

In the concurrency test, have each worker call the real installer.getGeneratedClasses() directly and return that method's actual result. Make getGeneratedClasses() package-private with the repository's visible-for-testing comment, and restore getTransformerForAsmVisitor() to private. This moves the test access to the initialization method where the publication race lives, without changing the production algorithm.

Assert each future's returned bundle is non-null and identical to the published bundle as the future is consumed. Remove the intermediate usedHelpers collection and second assertion pass. Import the nested GeneratedClasses type rather than repeatedly qualifying it. Remove the per-worker transformer construction, callback, AtomicReference capture, and imports no longer needed. Rename the concurrency test if needed so it describes direct concurrent initialization rather than transformations.

Keep generatesAndReusesHelpersOnlyWhenTransforming exercising real Byte Buddy transformations and proving deferred generation and reuse. Retain the concurrent start barrier, bounded waits, and executor shutdown/termination checks. Preserve the regression against returning a losing initializer's unpublished bundle: do not replace each worker's actual return value with a later read of installer.generatedClasses. Do not introduce another helper or test abstraction merely to reduce lines.

Limit this change to the test simplification and necessary production access adjustments. Preserve the lazy-generation/CAS algorithm, class-loading safety, helper injection ordering and fallback semantics. Do not change benchmark code, other PRs, block-comment style, configuration, PR title/description, or draft/base state. Do not create another PR or post replies to human reviewers.

Apply :javaagent-tooling:spotlessApply directly before focused behavior validation. Run :javaagent-tooling:unitTests, including supported-Java coverage with -PtestJavaVersion=8 where feasible, and report actual outcomes or blockers. Keep the existing Byte Buddy runtime exclusions and do not clean, bypass caches, or force task reruns.

replies.body: Implemented in `5bf45025`. The concurrency test now returns each direct `getGeneratedClasses()` result and checks it against the published instance; real-transformation laziness and reuse coverage remains. Spotless and unit tests passed on default Java and with `-PtestJavaVersion=8`.
